sections.title: What This Module Covers
sections.body: This module covers authentication in Rails at the fresher level. You will learn: Devise as the most commonly used Rails authentication gem (what it provides out of the box, the key helpers like current_user, user_signed_in?, before_action :authenticate_user!), the difference between sessions (server-side state) and cookies (client-side), how HTTP sessions work in Rails (session hash, cookie-based session store, CSRF protection), and an introduction to token-based authentication (JWT concept, the Authorization header, stateless vs stateful auth, and why APIs prefer tokens over sessions).

sections.title: Key Concepts at a Glance
sections.body: Devise: gem 'devise' in Gemfile. rails generate devise:install then rails generate devise User creates User model with email/password. Migrations add encrypted_password, reset_password_token, remember_created_at columns. Helpers: current_user returns logged-in user or nil. user_signed_in? returns boolean. before_action :authenticate_user! in controller locks down actions. Sessions: HTTP is stateless. Rails session hash is stored in a signed cookie. session[:user_id] = user.id to log in. session.clear to log out. CSRF: Rails generates authenticity_token and validates it on non-GET requests. Cookies: cookies[:key] = value. Signed: cookies.signed[:key]. Encrypted: cookies.encrypted[:key]. Token auth: Client sends token in Authorization: Bearer <token> header. Server validates token and identifies user. JWT (JSON Web Token) is the most common format. No server-side session storage needed — good for APIs. Devise-JWT and simple_token_auth are common gems.

sections.title: What Interviewers Ask Freshers
sections.body: Key authentication fresher questions: (1) What does Devise provide out of the box? (2) What is the difference between current_user and user_signed_in?? (3) What is a session and how does Rails implement it? (4) What is the difference between a session and a cookie? (5) What is CSRF and how does Rails protect against it? (6) What is token-based authentication and when would you use it over session-based auth? (7) What is JWT? What are its three parts? (8) How do you protect a controller action so only logged-in users can access it? (9) What is the difference between authentication and authorization? (10) What happens when a user logs out in a session-based system vs a token-based system?
